title: Incident Bot v2 Slack context cards: layout hierarchy, truncation, drill-down, accessibility
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Goal
Define the Slack layout for Incident Bot v2 “context cards” so responders can scan the first message in #incidents/#eng-oncall in <30s, then drill down without flooding the thread. This ticket covers:
- Card hierarchy and order
- Truncation rules (message + modal)
- Drill-down behavior (buttons, modals, pagination)
- Accessibility requirements (readability, keyboard/screen reader expectations within Slack constraints)

Non-goals
- Defining the underlying data schema (see diag-context payload draft)
- Picking exact thresholds/wording of signal interpretation (owned by SRE/telemetry)

Primary users
- On-call engineer in a high-stress incident (mobile + desktop)
- SRE incident lead doing rapid triage and handoffs

Proposed message structure (top-level)
Slack message = “Incident Context (v2)” with 3 primary cards in this order:
1) Deploy context (fastest correlation)
2) Config changes (common root cause, but may be redacted)
3) Saturation signals (capacity/queue/KV cache)

Rationale: responders most frequently ask “what changed?” first, then “did config/routing change?”, then “are we saturated?”.

Card visual hierarchy (Block Kit)
- Each card starts with a short header line using plain text (avoid color-only semantics). Example:
  - “Deploy context — OK” / “Deploy context — WARN” / “Deploy context — UNKNOWN”
- Header is followed by 3–6 bullet rows (Section block) of the most decision-relevant fields.
- Use code formatting for identifiers (service, version, commit SHA) and metric values.
- Use a consistent “Links” row at the end of each card with deep links (Console dashboards, deploy view, traces/logs). Keep links to max 3 per card to reduce visual noise.

Recommended card contents (summary view)
1) Deploy context (summary)
- Service: `hosted-api` / `router` / etc.
- Current version/image: short SHA prefix (e.g., `a1b2c3d`)
- Rollout phase: `canary` | `rolling` | `complete` | `rollback`
- Last deploy window: relative time (“7m ago”, “2h ago”)
- Canary health (if available): `pass` / `fail` / `n/a`
- Links: “Deploy timeline”, “Related PRs”, “Runbook: deploy triage”

2) Config changes (summary)
- Scope: tenant/route/region (as applicable)
- Change count: e.g., “3 changes (1 redacted)”
- Show only top N changed keys with before/after preview (see truncation rules)
- Include explicit redaction disclosure: “Some values redacted for safety. Use ‘View full diff’ for safe expanded view; request elevated access if needed.”
- Links: “Open in Console (diff)”, “Routing policy view”, “Runbook: config diff”

3) Saturation signals (summary)
- Region/pool: `us-east`, `dedicated:acme-prod`, etc.
- GPU util (p95 or max as defined by telemetry standards): show value + short qualifier (e.g., “92% (high)”)
- Queue depth / admission control: show value and whether backpressure is active
- KV cache pressure: show value and whether evictions increasing
- “Top suspected bottleneck” (single-line heuristic) if available; otherwise omit to avoid false confidence
- Links: “Saturation dashboard”, “Error budget burn”, “Trace samples”

Truncation + pagination rules
Constraints to design for:
- Slack messages become unreadable quickly; keep summary scannable.
- Slack Block Kit has practical limits; avoid large diffs directly in-message.
- Must work on mobile.

Global rules
- Summary message should target <= ~25 blocks total (hard cap varies, but keep conservative).
- Never print raw secrets; even in modals assume shared channel visibility.
- Prefer “show fewer + drill down” vs “dump everything”.

Config diff truncation (summary)
- Show at most 5 changed keys in the card summary.
- For each key, show a single-line preview:
  - `key_path`: `old_value` → `new_value`
- Value truncation:
  - Strings: truncate at 80 characters; append “…”
  - Arrays/objects: show “{…}” or “[ … ]” with item count when known
- Always include an action: “View full diff” (opens modal).

Modal diff view (drill-down)
- Modal includes:
  - Title: “Config diff (safe view)”
  - Scope line (tenant/route/region/time)
  - Paginated list of changes (10 per page)
  - Each row uses a fixed format:
    - `key_path`
    - Before (truncated to 200 chars)
    - After (truncated to 200 chars)
    - Redaction state: “REDACTED” label when applicable
- Provide “Next” / “Previous” buttons and a “Copy as text” action (copies a safe, redacted snippet).

Saturation signals truncation
- Summary shows at most 6 metrics: GPU util, queue depth, backpressure/admission, KV cache pressure, scheduler latency/backlog, regional capacity headroom (as available).
- If additional metrics exist, show “+N more signals” with “View details” action.

Modal saturation view
- Modal includes:
  - A “Now vs 15m ago” row for each signal if available (responders like directionality).
  - Keep formatting minimal: two columns as text; avoid charts.
  - Pagination if >12 rows.

Deploy context truncation
- Summary shows last 2 deploy events (current + previous) if available.
- “View deploy history” opens modal with last 10 events (time, version, phase, canary result).

Drill-down behavior and interaction model
- Buttons must be idempotent and safe to retry (eng requirement, but affects UX).
- Primary actions (per card):
  - Deploy context: “View deploy history”
  - Config changes: “View full diff”
  - Saturation: “View signal details”
- Secondary actions:
  - “Open dashboard” deep links (Console/observability)
  - “Copy commands” (safe CLI queries) where applicable
- When data is missing or times out:
  - Show “UNKNOWN” state in header and a single line explaining why (e.g., “Telemetry query timed out (5s).”) plus links to dashboards.
  - Avoid “empty card with no text”.

Accessibility requirements
- Do not rely on color to convey severity. Use explicit text labels: OK/WARN/CRITICAL/UNKNOWN.
- Keep headers and labels short; avoid jargon where possible.
- Ensure link text is descriptive (“Open saturation dashboard”) vs raw URLs.
- Buttons must have clear verbs and objects (“View full diff”, not “View”).
- Keep consistent ordering across cards so screen readers and scanning users can build a mental model.
- Support dark mode by avoiding custom color assumptions; default Slack styling only.

Open questions (resolved in comments)
- Whether to include an overall “At a glance” mini-summary above cards (decision: no; too noisy and often wrong without full context).
- Whether to include per-tenant identifiers in-channel (decision: only safe tenant slug if already used in incident channel norms; otherwise show internal incident ID and provide deep link).

Acceptance criteria
- A single pinned design spec (this ticket) describing summary layout and modal drill-down for all three cards.
- Concrete truncation limits documented (N rows, char limits, pagination size).
- Accessibility guidance included (non-color semantics, descriptive links/buttons).
- Aligns with bot degraded-mode behavior (still useful with timeouts; shows links).

References
- Drive mock examples: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/bot-ux-mock-thread-examples.json
- Incident context collection guidelines: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/incident-context-collection-guidelines.json
- Related eng tickets: ENG-5425 (Slack interactions ack/retry), ENG-5422 (diff redaction), ENG-5427 (telemetry cache)
comments: 2025-02-19 (Marissa Cole): Please keep the first message scannable. In prior incidents responders complained the bot was “too chatty” and buried human updates. Hard requirement: summary view must not exceed a single screen on desktop.

2025-02-20 (Miles Thornton): Agree on order (deploy > config > saturation). Also: degraded mode is important—if telemetry is timing out we still need the bot to produce links + explain what failed, not just omit the section.

2025-02-21 (Aisha Bello): For accessibility + correctness: avoid fancy severity icons; use OK/WARN/CRITICAL/UNKNOWN. Also please don’t invent interpretations in the UI that look like a diagnosis unless we’re very confident.

2025-02-24 (Devon Price): Proposed Block Kit approach: one message with dividers between cards; each card uses a Section with fields where possible, then a final Actions block with 2–3 buttons. Large diffs go to modals with pagination (10/page).
2025-02-25 (Allison Grant): Saturation card should show directionality if we can (now vs 15m ago). Even just “92% → 95%” is enough; charts are unnecessary and hard to read in Slack.

2025-02-27 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Reminder: any config diff in Slack must be safe even if someone shares a screenshot. Redaction disclosure needs to be explicit. We should also avoid showing tenant IDs unless already approved; use safe slug or link out.
2025-03-03 (Marissa Cole): Approved with one change: keep links row to max 3 links per card. If more are needed, put the extras behind ‘More links’ in the modal to reduce clutter.
2025-03-06 (Devon Price): Implemented in mocks and shared with eng. Follow-up: DES-205 for redaction warning + “request elevated access” copy in modal.
activity: 2025-02-24: Draft truncation + modal pagination rules added
2025-03-06: Marked Done; handed off to ENG-5425 / bot implementation
